intended_object: The reduction-mod-I homomorphism from the torsion subgroup of the unit group (𝓞_K)ˣ (the roots of unity of K) to the unit group (𝓞_K/I)ˣ, sending ζ to ζ mod I. Taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body applies `Units.map` to the quotient map `𝓞 K → 𝓞 K ⧸ I`, which gives (𝓞 K)ˣ →* (𝓞 K ⧸ I)ˣ, and then restricts it to the subgroup `Units.torsion K`. The definition of `Units.torsion K` was not opened; from its name, the docstring and how the file uses it (`rootsOfUnity_eq_torsion`), it is the torsion subgroup of (𝓞 K)ˣ. The result is exactly the map ζ ↦ ζ mod I on the roots of unity of K, and the companion simp lemma `torsionMapQuot_apply` confirms this by `rfl`. The file uses the map as intended: it proves the map is injective when the ideal norm is coprime to the torsion order, and from that derives that the norm is congruent to 1 modulo the torsion order. The construction lives in the number-field setting (`𝓞 K`, `Units.torsion K`), and the parallel general version for roots of unity of any given order is `Ideal.rootsOfUnityMapQuot` in the same file. The definition does not add any hypothesis (the `[NumberField K]` instance is introduced only after it), so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no separate declaration for this exact map.
